text:
maria: Heads-up — during Glacial v1 bring-up with the q5 quant bundle we saw notable locale variance. zh/ja longform BLEU down ~6 pts on multi-paragraph samples, and an Arabic RTL bracket/mirroring flip in mid-sentence. anyone triaging? :thinking:

jing: I reproduced on staging. Quick repro: `scripts/eval_locale.sh --model glacial-v1 --quant q5 --locales zh,ja,ar --suite longform` — produces consistent drops on the longform suite.

sam: can you paste one failing example (orig -> new) so i can start a bisect?

maria: sure — short example below (baseline float32 -> glacial-q5):
```
IN: zh multi-paragraph input...
BASELINE_OUT: 他们说：“我们会在明天交付。”
GLACIAL_Q5_OUT: 他们 说: “我们 在 明 天 交 付 .”  
```

axel: that looks like a tokenization/segmentation regression — whitespace inserted between multi-byte graphemes. for ja i see furigana/kanji adjacency splitting unexpectedly. tokenizer config we use during quant offline step uses `normalize=nfkc` + `keep_zwsp=false` — could that mismatch with the runtime preproc? @jing

jing: checked token ids for the failing zh sample. pre-quant vs post-quant token ids diverge starting around U+3000 and for sequences containing ZWJ/U+200D. not purely a rounding noise — actual segmentation boundary shifts. i'll dump tokenization traces to /tmp/glacial-tokenlogs.tar.gz.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deploy glacial-v1-q5 to staging-a finished (build glacial-20260322-3).

sam: can we confirm float32 parity? if float32 -> glacial float weights keep parity, then it's likely quant kernel/path causing detokenization mismatch. i'll run a float32 vs q5 parity pass on the same checkpoint.

maria: running parity now, posting numbers soon.

maria: quick numbers: float32 run vs baseline: BLEU 28.4 -> 27.9 (small). q5 run: BLEU 28.4 -> 22.1 (huge). so quantization is the main delta.

axel: ok that nails it to quant. proposed next steps: 1) per-layer activation distribution comparison (pre/post quant) for failing samples; 2) run tokenizer preproc with `keep_zwsp=true` and `normalization=kc` to see if normalization step explains split; 3) short kernel bisect q5->q4 to find which quant recipe change triggers the split.

jing: i'll take step 2 and upload sanitized token traces. sam/axel can you set up a minimal kernel smoke test to reproduce segmentation at token id level? i'll point you to the failing samples.

sam: on it, ETA ~2h for a reproducible kernel test harness.

maria: adding a canary guard to the regression suite and blocking rollout until we either fix or autos-rollback. cc @eng-sre for rollback hook. :lock:

axel: also add a localized unit test (ja/zh/ar) containing the specific multi-paragraph and bracket-edge cases so this doesn't slip through again.

maria: thanks all — keeping this thread as the triage log. please post logs/links here when available. :thumbsup:
